name: s1: Simple test-time scaling
authors: Niklas Muennighoff, Zitong Yang, Weijia Shi, Xiang Lisa Li et al. (Stanford University; co-authored with University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI, Contextual AI)
venue: EMNLP 2025 (Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pp. 20275-20321); originally arXiv:2501.19393, Jan 2025
code_url: https://github.com/simplescaling/s1 (model, data s1K, and code open-source; s1-32B weights and s1K-1.1 dataset released)
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique elicited via decoding-time intervention: 'budget forcing' suppresses the end-of-thinking token and appends 'Wait' to force the model to continue thinking, which leads it to double-check and self-correct its in-progress reasoning; not a learned critic and not tool-verified.
feedback_source: self-generated. There is no external verifier, unit test, oracle label, or environment reward at inference time; the extra 'Wait'-induced thinking is the model re-examining its own reasoning. (Training signal is SFT on Gemini-distilled reasoning traces, also not verifier-gated.)
iteration_structure: iterative-refine via sequential test-time scaling: the model generates a single long reasoning trace whose length is controlled by budget forcing; appending 'Wait' 2/4/6 times forces additional self-correction rounds within one trajectory (the authors classify this as sequential, not parallel, scaling, contrasting it with majority voting).
reflection_object: reasoning chain (the in-progress chain-of-thought / 'thinking' segment): budget forcing forces the model to keep extending and revising its current reasoning trace, often fixing incorrect intermediate steps before committing to a final answer. Secondarily the method modifies model weights once via SFT on 1,000 reasoning traces, but the test-time self-correction operates on the reasoning chain itself.
requires_training: SFT (supervised fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct on the 1,000-example s1K reasoning-trace dataset; ~26 minutes on 16 H100 GPUs). The self-correction/test-time-scaling behavior at inference is in-context (no weight update); budget forcing is a decoding-time intervention requiring no further training.
reward_or_critic_model: none. No reward model or trained critic is used. Reasoning traces for SFT are distilled from Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking Experimental; the model self-corrects at test time without any external judge. Self-as-judge only in the implicit sense that the model re-examines its own reasoning when forced to continue.
distillation_target: model-weights (reasoning ability distilled from Gemini Thinking traces into Qwen2.5-32B via SFT on s1K). The test-time self-correction itself is not distilled into a reusable artifact; it is elicited live by the budget-forcing decoding rule.
emergent_vs_engineered: scaffold/decoding-engineered. Unlike R1's RL-emergent 'aha'/self-verification, s1's self-correction is hand-engineered: a hard-coded decoding intervention that appends the literal string 'Wait' (and suppresses the end-of-thinking delimiter) to force the model to reconsider. The underlying reasoning capability is hypothesized to be latent from pretraining and merely 'activated' by 1K-example SFT (Superficial Alignment Hypothesis, a la LIMA).
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad. The long reasoning trace ('thinking' tokens) within a single problem acts as the scratchpad; there is no persistent episodic memory, skill library, or playbook.
memory_persistence: within-episode. Self-correction happens within a single problem's reasoning trace; nothing is carried across problems or sessions (the SFT-encoded knowledge is in weights, not an explicit memory store).
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a. No memory store is maintained or curated. (The closest analogue is data curation of s1K itself: the 59K candidate pool is filtered down to 1,000 via the Quality/Difficulty/Diversity selection algorithm, but this is training-data curation, not run-time memory curation.)
error_localization_granularity: step-level (within the reasoning chain): budget forcing makes the model revisit and revise individual intermediate reasoning steps mid-trace (e.g., it tries to stop after '...is 2.' but the forced 'Wait' makes it re-derive and correct that step). The control/scaling is measured at the trace/token-budget (outcome) level, but the self-correction itself targets reasoning steps.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task. Self-correction and refinement occur within a single problem's reasoning trace via additional test-time compute; there is no transfer of experience across tasks at inference.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery. By forcing the model to keep thinking ('Wait') instead of terminating, s1 lets the model correct errors in-flight within the same reasoning trajectory (the paper shows it 'double-check[s] its answer, often fixing incorrect reasoning steps'), rather than retrying in a fresh episode.
task_domains: math (competition math) and QA/reasoning (PhD-level science questions). Specifically reasoning-intensive tasks; no code, web-navigation, embodied, or dialogue domains.
benchmarks: AIME 2024 (AIME24), MATH500, GPQA Diamond (198 PhD-level science questions). Ablations also use these three; data decontaminated against them with 8-gram matching.
headline_result: After SFT on s1K (1,000 examples) + budget forcing, s1-32B exceeds o1-preview on competition math by up to 27% (MATH500 and AIME24). Test-time scaling via budget forcing extrapolates AIME24 from 50% (no intervention) to 57%. Final s1-32B: AIME24 56.7%, MATH500 93.0%, GPQA Diamond 59.6% (vs base Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 26.7 / 84.0 / 49.0).
baselines: Base model Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (no reasoning SFT); s1 w/o budget forcing (1K SFT only); API reasoning models o1-preview / o1-mini / o1 and Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking; open-weight reasoning models QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-r1 (>=800K examples) and r1-distill (800K); open-data SFT replications Sky-T1 (17K) and Bespoke-32B (17K). Alternative test-time scaling methods: token-conditional control (TCC), step-conditional control (SCC), class-conditional control (CCC), rejection sampling (RS), and parallel majority voting.
gains_vs_baseline: vs base Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct: AIME24 +30.0 pts (26.7 -> 56.7), MATH500 +9.0 pts (84.0 -> 93.0), GPQA +10.6 pts (49.0 -> 59.6). Budget forcing alone adds +6.7 pts on AIME24 over s1 w/o BF (50.0 -> 56.7). s1-32B beats o1-preview (AIME24 44.6, GPQA 73.3, MATH500 85.5) on AIME24 and MATH500 'by up to 27%' but trails o1-preview on GPQA. Matches/exceeds the open-data Sky-T1 (AIME24 43.3) and is competitive with Bespoke-32B (63.3) using only 1K vs 17K examples; data-efficiency is the key gain. Ablation: 'Wait' 1x->2x->4x raises AIME24 53.3->53.3 -> 56.7 region; training on the full 59K pool gives no substantial gain over the 1K selection, and random/longest-only/diversity-only selection is ~-30% on AIME24.
compute_cost_profile: Training: extremely cheap, ~26 minutes of SFT on 16 H100 GPUs on 1,000 examples (no RL, no reward model) -- vs R1's >=800K examples and RL. Inference: budget forcing increases test-time compute by forcing more thinking tokens (e.g., forcing the model not to stop 2/4/6 times); AIME24 best point uses ~7,320 thinking tokens (f(7320)=57%). Sequential scaling is bounded -- it eventually flattens and is capped by the model's context window. Parallel majority voting is also evaluated (2-64 samples).
known_limitations: Budget forcing has two stated key limitations when scaling further: (1) performance eventually flattens out (does not monotonically reach 100%), and (2) it is constrained by the underlying model's context window. Repeatedly appending 'Wait' yields diminishing/inverse returns past a point. Rejection sampling shows an inverse scaling trend (longer samples are more often wrong). The method is evaluated only on math/science reasoning; gains depend heavily on the latent reasoning ability of the strong Qwen2.5-32B base (Superficial Alignment Hypothesis) and on high-quality distilled traces from Gemini. Evaluation is also sensitive to non-determinism in vLLM runs.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only / self-verify. At test time s1 uses NO external verifier, oracle label, environment reward, or tool feedback -- the model self-corrects purely by being forced to keep thinking. This is a notable contrast to oracle-dependent self-correction critiques (Huang et al., Kamoi et al.): s1's gains come without label leakage, but only because the extra forced computation lets a strong model exploit its own latent reasoning, and the effect is modest and saturating.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive but task-dependent and saturating. Forcing more thinking via 'Wait' improves competition-math/GPQA accuracy without any oracle (e.g., AIME24 50%->57%), and the paper explicitly reports it 'often fix[es] incorrect reasoning steps'. However, gains flatten with more forced 'Wait's and the related rejection-sampling variant shows inverse scaling, so unbounded self-correction is not net-positive.
calibration_effect: not-measured. The paper measures task accuracy and controllability/scaling slope of test-time compute, not confidence calibration or a 'reasoning tax'; calibration effects of budget forcing are not reported.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a. s1 is a method/model for eliciting test-time scaling and self-correction, not a failure-attribution or failure-classification system; it does not classify failure modes, attribute responsible agents, or localize failing steps as a diagnostic output.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets 'underthinking' / premature termination of reasoning: by suppressing the end-of-thinking token and appending 'Wait', budget forcing prevents the model from stopping too early and induces deeper reasoning and in-flight self-correction. The flip side (saturation and inverse scaling from over-forcing 'Wait') exposes an 'overthinking'-style failure where additional forced reasoning no longer helps or hurts.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes -- s1K: 1,000 curated questions paired with reasoning traces and solutions (distilled from Gemini Thinking), plus the underlying 59K-example candidate pool, the s1-32B model weights, and full code. An improved s1.1 model and s1K-1.1 dataset (R1-distilled traces) were also released.
builds_on: OpenAI o1 (test-time scaling, the target being replicated); Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (base model); Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking Experimental (source of distilled reasoning traces); LIMA / Superficial Alignment Hypothesis (Zhou et al. 2023, motivating 1K-example sufficiency); test-time-compute scaling literature (Snell et al. 2024; Brown et al. 2024 on repeated/parallel sampling); lm-evaluation-harness (Gao et al.). Conceptually parallel to DeepSeek-R1 and Kimi k1.5 (RL-based o1 replications) which it contrasts against.
extended_by_or_inspired: Spawned a wave of sample-efficient reasoning-SFT and test-time-scaling work and is a canonical reference/baseline for o1/R1-era reasoning replication and inference-time control. Direct successors include the authors' own s1.1 (R1-distilled traces) and the broader 'budget forcing'/controllable-thinking-budget line of work; frequently cited alongside LIMO ('Less is More for Reasoning') and other 1K-scale reasoning-distillation efforts. (Specific named downstream papers not enumerated in the source; treated as inspiring the controllable-test-time-compute and minimal-SFT-reasoning literature.)
citation_count: approx. 1,271 (Semantic Scholar, CorpusID:276079693, as of June 2026); Google Scholar lists ~1,255 for the s1 entry. Reference count 98.
reasoning_model_native: Yes -- s1 explicitly targets o1/R1-style reasoning models with an explicit 'thinking' phase; it both creates such a model (s1-32B has a thinking segment delimited by an end-of-thinking token) and controls it. Budget forcing presupposes a model that emits a separable thinking trace, so the method is native to reasoning models and would not apply to non-thinking LLMs without that structure.
on_policy_distillation_link: Off-policy SFT distillation, not on-policy distillation: s1 distills static reasoning traces from a teacher (Gemini Thinking) into Qwen2.5-32B via standard supervised fine-tuning on a fixed 1K dataset -- the student does not generate its own rollouts that are then graded/relabeled. It is the data-efficiency counterpoint to on-policy distillation / RL approaches (DeepSeek-R1), showing that minimal off-policy SFT plus a decoding-time intervention rivals RL-trained reasoners; relevant to OPD discussions as the 'simple SFT + test-time control' baseline.
sample_efficiency: Extremely high training sample efficiency: only 1,000 SFT examples (s1K) suffice to make Qwen2.5-32B competitive with o1-preview, vs >=800K examples for r1/r1-distill and 17K for Sky-T1/Bespoke-32B; training on the full 59K pool gives no substantial gain over the 1K selection. Test-time: budget forcing's gain (AIME24 50->57%) comes from a single trace extended with ~2-6 forced 'Wait's; majority voting uses up to 64 samples for the parallel baseline.
